$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the report reprocessing policy (KAN-7).
Imported by the web app (src/domain/retry.ts) and by the Cloud Functions
Processing runs once, from a Storage trigger declared with retry:false —
a rate-limited model call, a cold provider or a trigger that fired before
the Firestore record existed leaves a report stranded with no way back.
The `retryReport` callable is that way back. It costs no upload operation
and no additional storage, so the only budget it spends is AI calls, and
The server decides; the browser only uses these numbers to decide whether
to offer the button. functions/src/retry.ts is the authority.
$maxComment: Retries only, on top of the automatic first run. Three is enough to ride
out a provider outage and few enough that a stuck report cannot quietly
$cooldownComment: Measured from the start of the previous attempt, not its end, so a retry
that genuinely took three minutes is not made to wait afterwards. This is
not concurrency control — the claim transaction handles that — it is what
stops a failure that returns instantly from burning the whole allowance
in the time it takes to click three times.
$staleComment: How long a report may sit in an in-flight status before the user is
allowed to restart it. Comfortably above the trigger's 540-second
timeout, so a run that is merely slow is never interrupted; anything
still in flight after this has lost its worker and will never finish.
$permanentComment: Failures where the same bytes will fail the same way, so the button is
not offered and the callable refuses. A scanned page will still be a
scanned page; a damaged PDF will still be damaged. Anything over quota
had its object deleted by usage.ts, so there is nothing left to read.
Notably absent: consent/ai-processing-missing. That one is the reason
this feature exists — the user agrees on the account page and the report
they already uploaded goes through, without spending a second upload.
Also absent: partially_processed. Retrying it would delete results the
user can already see, in exchange for a re-read that may do worse. If
that becomes wanted, it needs to write the new results before dropping
the old ones, not reuse this path.
